A.summary: Best copper of the four: zero-skew coupled pairs over ground, plane cut-outs under the connector pads, pours for +3V3 and +12V, 115 ground vias, clean DRC. Held back by a blocker: no M.2 retention notch or half-hole at (186.2, 98.76), so the card cannot be screwed down as fabricated.

B.summary: Not orderable: ten GND pads are unconnected (J2 fingers 9/21/27/33/39/45/51, J1 A15/A27/A28), the PCIe pairs are uncoupled and split across layers over plane voids, and +3V3 runs on a single 0.6 mm track of about 37 mm through single vias.

C.summary: The only board with no blocking defect: clean DRC, zero-skew coupled pairs over ground, plane-fed power with via arrays, retention half-hole present. Weaker points are the three-way In1 split near the layer transitions, no pad relief under J1, a thin 0.35 mm half-hole land and needless via-size variety.

D.summary: Two unbroken ground planes and the tidiest pair routing, with a proper 5.5 mm retention half-hole. But the slot's +3V3 is fed through two 0.25 mm tracks of about 15 mm, the lanes are length-matched with tight serpentines PCIe does not need, and one unwaived edge-clearance DRC error remains.

human_guess.why: D's half-hole via has a legacy-format UUID at an off-grid position whose perpendicular foot on the slanted board edge is exactly the stale DRC exclusion marker in the project file, so it is the original via; C has the same UUID placed on the marker coordinate with a custom rule, which looks reverse-engineered. D also uses KiCad GUI default zone values (0.508/0.254 mm), a multi-layer zone, tuner-style arc serpentines, no via on a round grid (0 of 92), and zero-length and duplicate segment leftovers.
